**Q1. What are the 10 most common Graph RAG failure modes and their signatures?**

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

@dataclass
class FailureMode:
    """Structured representation of a Graph RAG failure mode."""
    symbol: str
    name: str
    layer: str           # extraction | graph | retrieval | generation | operational
    symptom: str         # What the user/engineer observes
    root_cause: str      # Why it happens
    detection_metric: str
    quick_fix: str
    permanent_fix: str

GRAPH_RAG_FAILURE_MODES = [
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🔍",
        name="Entity Extraction Miss",
        layer="extraction",
        symptom="Queries about known entities return 'I don't know' despite documents existing",
        root_cause="LLM extraction missed entity due to ambiguous phrasing or domain jargon",
        detection_metric="Entity recall < 0.7 on eval set",
        quick_fix="Re-index with max_gleanings=2, add domain terms to entity_types",
        permanent_fix="Fine-tune extraction model on domain-specific entity examples"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🔗",
        name="Relationship Extraction Failure",
        layer="extraction",
        symptom="Graph has entities but almost no edges; traversal returns only seed node",
        root_cause="Relationships extracted within chunks but cross-chunk edges missed",
        detection_metric="Average entity degree < 2 in constructed graph",
        quick_fix="Add co-occurrence step for cross-chunk entity pairs",
        permanent_fix="Implement cross-document relationship extraction with shared entity registry"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🌀",
        name="Entity Duplication / Fragmentation",
        layer="graph",
        symptom="'Apple Inc' and 'Apple' are separate nodes with different information",
        root_cause="No entity resolution — same real-world entity has multiple graph nodes",
        detection_metric="Fuzzy duplicate ratio > 5% of entities",
        quick_fix="Post-extraction fuzzy merge (rapidfuzz threshold=85)",
        permanent_fix="Entity resolution pipeline: rule → fuzzy → embedding → LLM"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🧠",
        name="Hallucination in Graph Context",
        layer="generation",
        symptom="Answer cites entities not in retrieved graph context; faithfulness < 0.6",
        root_cause="LLM uses pretraining knowledge instead of staying grounded in context",
        detection_metric="Faithfulness < 0.7 on LLM-as-judge evaluation",
        quick_fix="Strengthen system prompt: 'ONLY use information from the graph context below'",
        permanent_fix="Citation-grounded generation: require entity name citations, post-validate"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="💥",
        name="Context Window Overflow",
        layer="retrieval",
        symptom="BFS expands too wide; LLM receives 30K+ tokens and ignores middle content",
        root_cause="Token budget not enforced; BFS not depth-limited",
        detection_metric="Context token count > model_max_tokens * 0.8",
        quick_fix="Add token budget cap to BFS traversal (stop when budget exceeded)",
        permanent_fix="Hierarchical context: entity summaries first, then text passages"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🦠",
        name="Community Drift (Stale Summaries)",
        layer="graph",
        symptom="Global search returns outdated information despite new document ingestion",
        root_cause="Community reports not regenerated after incremental updates",
        detection_metric="Community report timestamp > document timestamp",
        quick_fix="Trigger community re-summarisation for affected communities on update",
        permanent_fix="Event-driven pipeline: document update → re-cluster affected community → re-summarise"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🐢",
        name="Traversal Timeout / High Latency",
        layer="retrieval",
        symptom="Queries take 10+ seconds; p95 latency unacceptable for user-facing product",
        root_cause="BFS traversal on dense subgraph; no depth limit; synchronous Neo4j calls",
        detection_metric="Latency p95 > 5000ms",
        quick_fix="Add max_depth=3, budget_limit=50 to BFS; use async Neo4j driver",
        permanent_fix="Pre-compute entity neighborhoods at index time; cache hot-path subgraphs"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="🎭",
        name="Mode Confusion (Wrong Query Mode)",
        layer="retrieval",
        symptom="Factual query uses global mode (community reports) → vague answer; thematic query uses local → misses big picture",
        root_cause="Static query routing; no query intent classification",
        detection_metric="Answer relevance < 0.6 despite correct context retrieved",
        quick_fix="Add query router: keyword-based local/global/hybrid routing",
        permanent_fix="ML query intent classifier trained on labelled query/mode pairs"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="💸",
        name="Cost Explosion",
        layer="operational",
        symptom="GraphRAG indexing costs $500+ per run; LLM API bills spike",
        root_cause="gpt-4o for all operations + max_gleanings=1 + no caching",
        detection_metric="Cost per document > $0.50",
        quick_fix="Switch to gpt-4o-mini; enable caching; reduce max_gleanings to 0",
        permanent_fix="Cost monitoring per pipeline stage; auto-downgrade model on budget overrun"
    ),
    FailureMode(
        symbol="⚖️",
        name="Retrieval Bias (Popular Entity Dominance)",
        layer="retrieval",
        symptom="High-degree entities (hubs) dominate every query; niche but relevant entities never surface",
        root_cause="PageRank/degree bias in entity importance scoring",
        detection_metric="Top-5 entities same across 80%+ of queries",
        quick_fix="Normalize entity scores by degree; add rarity bonus for low-degree entities",
        permanent_fix="Personalized PageRank seeded from query embedding; diversity-aware re-ranking"
    )
]

def diagnose_failure(symptom: str) -> list[FailureMode]:
    """Find matching failure modes for a given symptom."""
    symptom_lower = symptom.lower()
    matches = [
        fm for fm in GRAPH_RAG_FAILURE_MODES
        if any(word in symptom_lower for word in fm.symptom.lower().split()[:5])
    ]
    return matches if matches else GRAPH_RAG_FAILURE_MODES
```

**Q2. How do you debug entity extraction failures (🔍)?**

```python
import asyncio
import json
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
import spacy

class EntityExtractionDebugger:
    """Debugging toolkit for entity extraction failures."""

    def __init__(self, llm: AsyncOpenAI):
        self.llm = llm
        try:
            self.nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_lg")
        except OSError:
            self.nlp = None

    async def audit_extraction(
        self,
        document_text: str,
        extracted_entities: list[str]
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Audit extraction quality: find entities that should have been found.
        """
        # Step 1: NER with spaCy as ground truth
        spacy_entities = []
        if self.nlp:
            doc = self.nlp(document_text[:10000])
            spacy_entities = [
                ent.text for ent in doc.ents
                if ent.label_ in {"ORG", "PERSON", "GPE", "PRODUCT", "EVENT"}
            ]

        extracted_lower = {e.lower().strip() for e in extracted_entities}
        spacy_lower = {e.lower().strip() for e in spacy_entities}

        # Entities spaCy found but LLM extraction missed
        missed_by_llm = spacy_lower - extracted_lower

        # Step 2: LLM validation of missed entities
        entity_validation = {}
        for entity in list(missed_by_llm)[:5]:  # Validate top 5 misses
            is_relevant = await self._check_entity_relevance(entity, document_text)
            entity_validation[entity] = is_relevant

        return {
            "spacy_entity_count": len(spacy_entities),
            "llm_entity_count": len(extracted_entities),
            "extraction_ratio": round(len(extracted_entities) / max(len(spacy_entities), 1), 2),
            "missed_by_llm": list(missed_by_llm)[:10],
            "validation": entity_validation,
            "recommendation": (
                "Set max_gleanings=2 to improve extraction"
                if len(missed_by_llm) > 5
                else "Extraction quality acceptable"
            )
        }

    async def _check_entity_relevance(
        self, entity_name: str, context: str
    ) -> bool:
        """Check if a missed entity is actually important."""
        prompt = f"""Is "{entity_name}" an important named entity in the following text that should be extracted for a knowledge graph?
Answer YES or NO only.

Text: {context[:500]}"""

        response = await self.llm.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o-mini",
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            max_tokens=5, temperature=0
        )
        return "YES" in response.choices[0].message.content.upper()

    def detect_low_density_graph(
        self, entities: list[str], relationships: list[tuple]
    ) -> dict:
        """Detect sparse graph (🔗 failure mode)."""
        import networkx as nx

        G = nx.DiGraph()
        G.add_nodes_from(entities)
        G.add_edges_from([(r[0], r[1]) for r in relationships])

        n_entities = G.number_of_nodes()
        n_edges = G.number_of_edges()
        avg_degree = (n_edges / max(n_entities, 1)) * 2

        isolated = [n for n in G.nodes() if G.degree(n) == 0]

        return {
            "n_entities": n_entities,
            "n_relationships": n_edges,
            "avg_degree": round(avg_degree, 2),
            "isolated_entities": len(isolated),
            "is_sparse": avg_degree < 2,
            "fix_needed": len(isolated) > n_entities * 0.3,
            "recommendation": (
                "Add cross-chunk co-occurrence relationship extraction"
                if avg_degree < 2 else "Graph density acceptable"
            )
        }
```

**Q3. How do you debug and fix entity duplication / fragmentation (🌀)?**

```python
from rapidfuzz import fuzz, process

class EntityDuplicationDebugger:
    """Detect and fix entity fragmentation in the knowledge graph."""

    def __init__(self, similarity_threshold: int = 85):
        self.threshold = similarity_threshold

    def find_potential_duplicates(
        self, entity_names: list[str]
    ) -> list[dict]:
        """
        Find entity name pairs that likely refer to the same real-world entity.
        Uses multiple fuzzy string matching strategies.
        """
        duplicates = []
        n = len(entity_names)

        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                name_a = entity_names[i]
                name_b = entity_names[j]

                # Multiple similarity measures
                simple_ratio = fuzz.ratio(name_a, name_b)
                sort_ratio = fuzz.token_sort_ratio(name_a, name_b)
                set_ratio = fuzz.token_set_ratio(name_a, name_b)

                # Take max similarity across strategies
                max_sim = max(simple_ratio, sort_ratio, set_ratio)

                if max_sim >= self.threshold:
                    duplicates.append({
                        "entity_a": name_a,
                        "entity_b": name_b,
                        "similarity": max_sim,
                        "strategy": "fuzzy_match",
                        "recommendation": f"Merge into canonical: {self._canonical_form(name_a, name_b)}"
                    })

        # Sort by similarity (highest first)
        return sorted(duplicates, key=lambda d: d["similarity"], reverse=True)

    def _canonical_form(self, name_a: str, name_b: str) -> str:
        """Choose canonical name: prefer longer, more descriptive form."""
        # Remove common abbreviation indicators
        clean_a = name_a.replace("Inc.", "").replace("Ltd.", "").strip()
        clean_b = name_b.replace("Inc.", "").replace("Ltd.", "").strip()
        # Prefer longer name (more specific)
        return name_a if len(clean_a) >= len(clean_b) else name_b

    def merge_duplicate_entities(
        self,
        entity_store: dict[str, dict],
        duplicates: list[dict]
    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
        """
        Merge duplicate entities into canonical forms.
        Preserves all relationships by redirecting edges.
        """
        # Build merge map: alias → canonical
        merge_map: dict[str, str] = {}
        for dup in duplicates:
            canonical = dup["recommendation"].replace("Merge into canonical: ", "")
            alias = dup["entity_b"] if canonical == dup["entity_a"] else dup["entity_a"]
            merge_map[alias] = canonical

        # Merge entity descriptions
        merged_store = {}
        for entity_name, entity_data in entity_store.items():
            canonical = merge_map.get(entity_name, entity_name)
            if canonical not in merged_store:
                merged_store[canonical] = entity_data.copy()
            else:
                # Merge descriptions
                existing_desc = merged_store[canonical].get("description", "")
                new_desc = entity_data.get("description", "")
                if new_desc and new_desc not in existing_desc:
                    merged_store[canonical]["description"] = (
                        existing_desc + " " + new_desc
                    )[:500]

        return merged_store, merge_map
```

**Q4. How do you debug hallucination in Graph RAG generation (🧠)?**

```python
import asyncio
import json
import re
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

class HallucinationDebugger:
    """
    Detect and prevent Graph RAG hallucinations.
    Key: answer must be grounded in retrieved graph context.
    """

    def __init__(self, llm: AsyncOpenAI):
        self.llm = llm

    def extract_entity_references(
        self, text: str, known_entities: set[str]
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Find entity names in answer text.
        Returns both grounded (in context) and ungrounded (hallucinated) references.
        """
        text_lower = text.lower()
        grounded = []
        ungrounded_candidates = []

        # Check each known entity
        for entity in known_entities:
            if entity.lower() in text_lower:
                grounded.append(entity)

        # Find proper nouns in answer NOT in known entities
        # Simple heuristic: capitalized sequences
        proper_nouns = re.findall(r'\b[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*\b', text)
        for noun in proper_nouns:
            if noun not in known_entities and len(noun) > 3:
                ungrounded_candidates.append(noun)

        return {
            "grounded_entities": grounded,
            "ungrounded_candidates": list(set(ungrounded_candidates))[:10],
            "grounding_ratio": len(grounded) / max(len(grounded) + len(ungrounded_candidates), 1)
        }

    async def generate_grounded_answer(
        self,
        query: str,
        graph_context: str,
        entities_in_context: list[str],
        max_tokens: int = 1000
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Generate answer with strict grounding instruction.
        Prevents LLM from using pretraining knowledge.
        """
        entity_list = ", ".join(entities_in_context[:20])

        system_prompt = f"""You are a precise question-answering system.
CRITICAL RULES:
1. ONLY use information from the graph context provided below.
2. Do NOT use any knowledge not present in the graph context.
3. If the context does not contain enough information, say "Based on the available context, I cannot fully answer this question."
4. When referencing entities, use EXACTLY these names: {entity_list}
5. Do not infer or assume relationships not explicitly stated in the context."""

        response = await self.llm.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o",
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"Graph Context:\n{graph_context}\n\nQuestion: {query}"}
            ],
            max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0
        )

        answer = response.choices[0].message.content

        # Validate grounding
        known_entities = set(entities_in_context)
        grounding_check = self.extract_entity_references(answer, known_entities)

        return {
            "answer": answer,
            "grounding_check": grounding_check,
            "is_grounded": grounding_check["grounding_ratio"] > 0.7
        }
```

**Q5. How do you detect and fix context window overflow (💥)?**

```python
import tiktoken
from typing import Iterator

class ContextOverflowDebugger:
    """
    Detect and prevent context window overflow in Graph RAG.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str = "gpt-4o-mini",
        max_context_tokens: int = 12000
    ):
        self.enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model)
        self.max_context_tokens = max_context_tokens

    def count_tokens(self, text: str) -> int:
        """Count tokens using tiktoken."""
        return len(self.enc.encode(text))

    def check_context_budget(
        self,
        entities: list[dict],
        relationships: list[dict],
        text_units: list[dict]
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Audit token budget before building context for LLM call.
        Identifies which section is consuming the most tokens.
        """
        entity_text = "\n".join([
            f"{e.get('name', '')}: {e.get('description', '')[:200]}"
            for e in entities
        ])
        rel_text = "\n".join([
            f"{r.get('source', '')} -> {r.get('target', '')}: {r.get('description', '')[:100]}"
            for r in relationships
        ])
        tu_text = "\n".join([str(t.get("text", ""))[:200] for t in text_units])

        entity_tokens = self.count_tokens(entity_text)
        rel_tokens = self.count_tokens(rel_text)
        tu_tokens = self.count_tokens(tu_text)
        total = entity_tokens + rel_tokens + tu_tokens

        return {
            "entity_tokens": entity_tokens,
            "relationship_tokens": rel_tokens,
            "text_unit_tokens": tu_tokens,
            "total_tokens": total,
            "budget": self.max_context_tokens,
            "overflow": total > self.max_context_tokens,
            "overflow_by": max(0, total - self.max_context_tokens),
            "recommendation": self._get_recommendation(
                entity_tokens, rel_tokens, tu_tokens, total
            )
        }

    def _get_recommendation(
        self,
        entity_t: int, rel_t: int, tu_t: int, total: int
    ) -> str:
        if total <= self.max_context_tokens:
            return "Within budget"
        dominant = max([("entities", entity_t), ("relationships", rel_t), ("text_units", tu_t)], key=lambda x: x[1])
        return f"Reduce {dominant[0]} ({dominant[1]} tokens). Use truncation or top-K selection."

    def build_budgeted_context(
        self,
        entities: list[dict],
        relationships: list[dict],
        text_units: list[dict],
        budget_tokens: int = 8000
    ) -> str:
        """Build context that strictly fits within token budget."""
        parts = []
        remaining = budget_tokens

        # Entities (30% budget)
        entity_budget = int(budget_tokens * 0.3)
        entity_text = "## Entities\n"
        for entity in entities:
            line = f"- **{entity.get('name', '')}**: {entity.get('description', '')[:150]}\n"
            line_tokens = self.count_tokens(line)
            if line_tokens > entity_budget:
                break
            entity_text += line
            entity_budget -= line_tokens
        parts.append(entity_text)
        remaining -= self.count_tokens(entity_text)

        # Relationships (30% budget)
        rel_budget = int(budget_tokens * 0.3)
        rel_text = "## Relationships\n"
        for rel in relationships:
            line = f"- {rel.get('source', '')} → {rel.get('target', '')}: {rel.get('description', '')[:100]}\n"
            line_tokens = self.count_tokens(line)
            if line_tokens > rel_budget:
                break
            rel_text += line
            rel_budget -= line_tokens
        parts.append(rel_text)
        remaining -= self.count_tokens(rel_text)

        # Text units (remaining budget)
        tu_text = "## Source Passages\n"
        for tu in text_units:
            passage = str(tu.get("text", ""))[:300]
            passage_tokens = self.count_tokens(passage)
            if passage_tokens > remaining:
                break
            tu_text += passage + "\n\n"
            remaining -= passage_tokens
        parts.append(tu_text)

        return "\n".join(parts)
```

**Q6. How do you detect and fix stale community summaries (🦠)?**

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import asyncio

class CommunityStalenessDetector:
    """Detect and refresh stale community reports in MS GraphRAG."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        communities_df,
        community_reports_df,
        max_age_days: int = 7
    ):
        self.communities = communities_df
        self.reports = community_reports_df
        self.max_age = max_age_days

    def find_stale_communities(self) -> list[str]:
        """Find communities with outdated reports."""
        import pandas as pd

        cutoff = datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=self.max_age)
        stale = []

        for _, report in self.reports.iterrows():
            report_date_str = report.get("created_at", "")
            if not report_date_str:
                stale.append(report.get("community_id", ""))
                continue

            try:
                report_date = datetime.fromisoformat(str(report_date_str).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
                if report_date.replace(tzinfo=None) < cutoff:
                    stale.append(report.get("community_id", ""))
            except (ValueError, AttributeError):
                stale.append(report.get("community_id", ""))

        return stale

    async def refresh_community_report(
        self,
        community_id: str,
        entity_descriptions: list[str],
        llm,
        model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"
    ) -> str:
        """Regenerate a single community report."""
        context = "\n".join(entity_descriptions[:20])

        response = await llm.chat.completions.create(
            model=model,
            messages=[{
                "role": "user",
                "content": f"""Summarize this community of related entities for a knowledge graph.
Include: key themes, important entities, notable relationships, and potential questions this community can answer.

Entities:
{context}

Provide a 2-3 paragraph summary."""
            }],
            max_tokens=500, temperature=0
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content

    async def refresh_stale_reports(
        self,
        entity_store: dict,
        llm,
        max_concurrent: int = 5
    ) -> dict:
        """Refresh all stale community reports."""
        stale_ids = self.find_stale_communities()
        if not stale_ids:
            return {"refreshed": 0, "stale_found": 0}

        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
        refreshed = 0

        async def refresh_one(community_id: str):
            nonlocal refreshed
            async with semaphore:
                # Get entities for this community
                community_entities = [
                    entity_store.get(name, {}).get("description", "")
                    for name in list(entity_store.keys())[:10]
                ]
                report = await self.refresh_community_report(
                    community_id, community_entities, llm
                )
                refreshed += 1
                return {"community_id": community_id, "report": report[:100]}

        await asyncio.gather(*[refresh_one(cid) for cid in stale_ids])

        return {"refreshed": refreshed, "stale_found": len(stale_ids)}
```

**Q7. How do you diagnose and fix traversal timeout / high latency (🐢)?**

```python
import asyncio
import time
from collections import deque

class TraversalLatencyDebugger:
    """Debug and fix graph traversal timeout issues."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        max_depth: int = 3,
        max_nodes: int = 50,
        timeout_seconds: float = 5.0
    ):
        self.max_depth = max_depth
        self.max_nodes = max_nodes
        self.timeout = timeout_seconds

    async def bfs_with_timeout(
        self,
        graph,
        seed_entities: list[str]
    ) -> dict:
        """
        BFS with hard timeout + node budget.
        Returns partial result on timeout rather than failing.
        """
        start_time = time.perf_counter()
        visited = set()
        queue = deque([(entity, 0) for entity in seed_entities])
        result_nodes = []
        timed_out = False
        budget_hit = False

        while queue:
            # Check timeout
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time
            if elapsed > self.timeout:
                timed_out = True
                break

            # Check node budget
            if len(result_nodes) >= self.max_nodes:
                budget_hit = True
                break

            node, depth = queue.popleft()

            if node in visited or depth > self.max_depth:
                continue

            visited.add(node)
            result_nodes.append(node)

            if depth < self.max_depth:
                # Get neighbours (async if using Neo4j)
                try:
                    neighbours = list(graph.neighbors(node))[:10]  # Limit fanout
                    queue.extend((n, depth + 1) for n in neighbours if n not in visited)
                except Exception:
                    continue

        latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000

        return {
            "nodes_retrieved": result_nodes,
            "latency_ms": round(latency_ms, 1),
            "timed_out": timed_out,
            "budget_hit": budget_hit,
            "nodes_count": len(result_nodes),
            "warning": "timed_out — partial result returned" if timed_out else None
        }

    def profile_graph_density(
        self, entity_name: str, graph
    ) -> dict:
        """Profile why traversal is slow for a specific entity."""
        try:
            degree = graph.degree(entity_name)
            in_degree = graph.in_degree(entity_name) if hasattr(graph, 'in_degree') else 0
            out_degree = graph.out_degree(entity_name) if hasattr(graph, 'out_degree') else 0

            # 2-hop neighbourhood size
            neighbours_1 = list(graph.neighbors(entity_name))
            n_2hop = sum(len(list(graph.neighbors(n))) for n in neighbours_1[:20])

            return {
                "entity": entity_name,
                "degree": degree,
                "1_hop_neighbours": len(neighbours_1),
                "estimated_2_hop": n_2hop,
                "is_hub": degree > 50,
                "recommendation": (
                    "Hub node — use degree-weighted sampling, not full BFS"
                    if degree > 50 else "Normal node — standard BFS is fine"
                )
            }
        except Exception as e:
            return {"entity": entity_name, "error": str(e)}
```

**Q8. How do you implement a comprehensive Graph RAG health check?**

```python
import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

@dataclass
class HealthCheckResult:
    """Result of a Graph RAG health check."""
    component: str
    status: str           # "ok" | "warning" | "critical"
    metric: str
    value: Any
    threshold: Any
    message: str
    fix: str = ""

class GraphRAGHealthChecker:
    """
    Automated health check for production Graph RAG systems.
    Covers all 10 failure modes.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        entity_store: dict,
        relation_store: dict,
        community_reports: list[dict],
        eval_results: dict | None = None
    ):
        self.entities = entity_store
        self.relations = relation_store
        self.reports = community_reports
        self.eval_results = eval_results or {}

    def check_all(self) -> list[HealthCheckResult]:
        """Run all health checks and return prioritized results."""
        checks = [
            self._check_entity_count(),
            self._check_graph_density(),
            self._check_entity_duplicates(),
            self._check_community_reports(),
            self._check_embedding_coverage(),
            self._check_retrieval_performance(),
            self._check_generation_quality(),
        ]
        # Sort by severity
        severity_order = {"critical": 0, "warning": 1, "ok": 2}
        return sorted(checks, key=lambda r: severity_order.get(r.status, 3))

    def _check_entity_count(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        n = len(self.entities)
        status = "ok" if n > 100 else ("warning" if n > 10 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Extraction", status=status,
            metric="entity_count", value=n, threshold=100,
            message=f"{n} entities extracted",
            fix="Increase max_gleanings, add domain entity_types" if status != "ok" else ""
        )

    def _check_graph_density(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        n_entities = len(self.entities)
        n_rels = len(self.relations)
        avg_degree = (n_rels / max(n_entities, 1)) * 2
        status = "ok" if avg_degree >= 2 else ("warning" if avg_degree >= 1 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Graph Structure", status=status,
            metric="avg_degree", value=round(avg_degree, 2), threshold=2.0,
            message=f"Average degree: {avg_degree:.2f}",
            fix="Add cross-chunk co-occurrence extraction" if status != "ok" else ""
        )

    def _check_entity_duplicates(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        from rapidfuzz import fuzz
        entity_names = list(self.entities.keys())
        if len(entity_names) < 2:
            return HealthCheckResult("Deduplication", "ok", "duplicates", 0, 0, "No duplicates")

        # Sample check (first 100 pairs)
        duplicate_count = 0
        for i in range(min(len(entity_names), 50)):
            for j in range(i + 1, min(len(entity_names), 50)):
                if fuzz.token_set_ratio(entity_names[i], entity_names[j]) > 85:
                    duplicate_count += 1

        ratio = duplicate_count / max(len(entity_names), 1)
        status = "ok" if ratio < 0.05 else ("warning" if ratio < 0.15 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Entity Resolution", status=status,
            metric="duplicate_ratio", value=round(ratio, 3), threshold=0.05,
            message=f"Estimated {duplicate_count} potential duplicates in sample",
            fix="Run EntityDuplicationDebugger.merge_duplicate_entities()" if status != "ok" else ""
        )

    def _check_community_reports(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        n = len(self.reports)
        if n == 0:
            return HealthCheckResult(
                "Community Reports", "critical", "report_count", 0, 1,
                "No community reports found",
                fix="Run graphrag index --root ./project to regenerate"
            )

        empty_reports = sum(
            1 for r in self.reports
            if not r.get("full_content") or len(str(r.get("full_content", ""))) < 50
        )
        ratio = empty_reports / n
        status = "ok" if ratio < 0.1 else ("warning" if ratio < 0.3 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Global Search", status=status,
            metric="empty_report_ratio", value=round(ratio, 3), threshold=0.1,
            message=f"{empty_reports}/{n} reports are empty",
            fix="Check LLM rate limits during indexing; regenerate reports" if status != "ok" else ""
        )

    def _check_embedding_coverage(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        entities_with_emb = sum(
            1 for e in self.entities.values()
            if e.get("embedding") is not None
        )
        coverage = entities_with_emb / max(len(self.entities), 1)
        status = "ok" if coverage > 0.95 else ("warning" if coverage > 0.7 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Embeddings", status=status,
            metric="embedding_coverage", value=round(coverage, 3), threshold=0.95,
            message=f"{entities_with_emb}/{len(self.entities)} entities have embeddings",
            fix="Check embedding API key and rate limits; re-run embedding step" if status != "ok" else ""
        )

    def _check_retrieval_performance(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        latency = self.eval_results.get("latency_p95_ms", 0)
        status = "ok" if latency < 2000 else ("warning" if latency < 5000 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Retrieval", status=status,
            metric="latency_p95_ms", value=latency, threshold=2000,
            message=f"p95 latency: {latency:.0f}ms",
            fix="Add max_depth=3, budget_limit=50 to BFS; use async Neo4j driver" if status != "ok" else ""
        )

    def _check_generation_quality(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        faithfulness = self.eval_results.get("faithfulness", 1.0)
        status = "ok" if faithfulness >= 0.8 else ("warning" if faithfulness >= 0.6 else "critical")
        return HealthCheckResult(
            component="Generation", status=status,
            metric="faithfulness", value=faithfulness, threshold=0.8,
            message=f"Faithfulness: {faithfulness:.2f}",
            fix="Strengthen system prompt grounding instruction; add citation validation" if status != "ok" else ""
        )
```

**Q9. How do you fix retrieval bias (⚖️) — hub entity dominance?**

```python
import networkx as nx
import numpy as np

def compute_diversity_aware_entity_scores(
    graph: nx.DiGraph,
    query_embedding: np.ndarray,
    entity_embeddings: dict[str, np.ndarray],
    top_k: int = 20
) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Diversity-aware entity scoring: prevents hub dominance.
    Combines semantic similarity, graph importance, and rarity bonus.
    """
    all_entities = list(entity_embeddings.keys())

    # 1. Semantic similarity scores
    emb_matrix = np.array([entity_embeddings[e] for e in all_entities])
    emb_matrix = emb_matrix / np.linalg.norm(emb_matrix, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    query_norm = query_embedding / np.linalg.norm(query_embedding)
    semantic_scores = emb_matrix @ query_norm

    # 2. Personalized PageRank (graph importance)
    try:
        personalization = {
            entity: float(score)
            for entity, score in zip(all_entities, semantic_scores)
            if entity in graph
        }
        ppr = nx.pagerank(graph, personalization=personalization, max_iter=100)
    except Exception:
        ppr = {entity: 1.0 / len(all_entities) for entity in all_entities}

    # 3. Degree-based rarity bonus (anti-hub measure)
    degrees = dict(graph.degree())
    max_degree = max(degrees.values(), default=1)

    scored_entities = []
    for i, entity in enumerate(all_entities):
        semantic = float(semantic_scores[i])
        importance = ppr.get(entity, 0.0)
        degree = degrees.get(entity, 0)

        # Rarity bonus: low-degree entities get boosted
        # Prevents hub nodes (degree=500) from always dominating
        rarity_bonus = 1.0 - (degree / max_degree) * 0.5  # 0.5-1.0

        # Combined score: weighted sum
        combined = (
            0.5 * semantic +
            0.3 * importance +
            0.2 * (1 - degree / max(max_degree, 1)) * rarity_bonus
        )

        scored_entities.append({
            "entity": entity,
            "semantic_score": round(semantic, 4),
            "ppr_score": round(importance, 6),
            "degree": degree,
            "rarity_bonus": round(rarity_bonus, 4),
            "combined_score": round(combined, 4)
        })

    # Sort by combined score
    scored_entities.sort(key=lambda x: x["combined_score"], reverse=True)
    return scored_entities[:top_k]
```

**Q10. How do you implement a comprehensive logging strategy for Graph RAG debugging?**

```python
import logging
import json
import time
import asyncio
from functools import wraps
from typing import Any, Callable

class GraphRAGStructuredLogger:
    """
    Structured logging for Graph RAG pipelines.
    Enables post-hoc debugging of failures.
    """

    def __init__(self, service_name: str = "graph_rag"):
        self.service = service_name
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(service_name)
        self._setup_json_handler()

    def _setup_json_handler(self) -> None:
        """Configure JSON structured logging."""
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
        formatter = logging.Formatter(
            '{"timestamp": "%(asctime)s", "level": "%(levelname)s", '
            '"service": "%(name)s", "message": %(message)s}'
        )
        handler.setFormatter(formatter)
        self.logger.addHandler(handler)
        self.logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    def log_query_start(
        self, query_id: str, query: str, mode: str
    ) -> None:
        payload = {"event": "query_start", "query_id": query_id,
                   "query": query[:100], "mode": mode}
        self.logger.info(json.dumps(payload))

    def log_retrieval_result(
        self, query_id: str,
        n_entities: int, n_relationships: int,
        context_tokens: int, latency_ms: float
    ) -> None:
        payload = {
            "event": "retrieval_complete", "query_id": query_id,
            "n_entities": n_entities, "n_relationships": n_relationships,
            "context_tokens": context_tokens, "latency_ms": latency_ms,
            "warning": "context_overflow" if context_tokens > 10000 else None
        }
        self.logger.info(json.dumps(payload))

    def log_generation_result(
        self, query_id: str, faithfulness: float,
        answer_tokens: int, latency_ms: float
    ) -> None:
        payload = {
            "event": "generation_complete", "query_id": query_id,
            "faithfulness": faithfulness, "answer_tokens": answer_tokens,
            "latency_ms": latency_ms,
            "alert": "low_faithfulness" if faithfulness < 0.7 else None
        }
        level = logging.WARNING if faithfulness < 0.7 else logging.INFO
        self.logger.log(level, json.dumps(payload))

    def log_failure(
        self, query_id: str, failure_mode: str,
        error: str, stage: str
    ) -> None:
        payload = {
            "event": "failure", "query_id": query_id,
            "failure_mode": failure_mode, "stage": stage,
            "error": error[:200]
        }
        self.logger.error(json.dumps(payload))

def log_graph_rag_call(logger: GraphRAGStructuredLogger):
    """Decorator to add structured logging to any Graph RAG function."""
    def decorator(func: Callable) -> Callable:
        @wraps(func)
        async def wrapper(*args, **kwargs) -> Any:
            import uuid
            query_id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
            start = time.perf_counter()

            try:
                result = await func(*args, **kwargs)
                latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
                logger.log_retrieval_result(
                    query_id, 0, 0, 0, latency_ms
                )
                return result
            except Exception as e:
                latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
                logger.log_failure(
                    query_id, "unknown", str(e), func.__name__
                )
                raise

        return wrapper
    return decorator
```

**S1. SCENARIO: 🧠 Production system faithfulness drops from 0.90 to 0.55 after corpus size tripled.**

*Root Cause:* Larger corpus → more retrieved entities → context window overflow → LLM uses pretraining fallback for missing context.

```python
async def diagnose_faithfulness_drop(
    rag_pipeline, test_queries: list[str], llm
) -> dict:
    """Diagnose faithfulness drop with full audit."""
    faithfulness_evaluator = GraphRAGFaithfulnessEvaluator(llm)
    results = []

    for query in test_queries[:10]:
        result = await rag_pipeline.query(query)
        faith = await faithfulness_evaluator.evaluate_faithfulness(
            result["answer"], result.get("context", "")
        )
        results.append({
            "query": query,
            "context_tokens": len(result.get("context", "").split()),
            "faithfulness": faith["faithfulness"],
            "ungrounded": faith.get("ungrounded_claims", 0)
        })

    # Find pattern: do high context_token queries have low faithfulness?
    import numpy as np
    tokens = [r["context_tokens"] for r in results]
    faiths = [r["faithfulness"] for r in results]

    correlation = np.corrcoef(tokens, faiths)[0, 1]
    return {
        "context_overflow_correlation": round(correlation, 3),
        "diagnosis": "context overflow causes faithfulness drop" if correlation < -0.5 else "other cause",
        "fix": "Reduce max_nodes in BFS to 30; use token-budgeted context builder"
    }
```

**S2–S10.** Key scenario patterns:

**S2. 🔍 Entity extraction misses all company names in financial documents.**

*Fix:* Financial docs use abbreviations (MSFT, AAPL). Add `entity_types: [company, ticker, fund, regulator]` to settings. Add few-shot examples with financial entity patterns to extraction prompt. Use domain-specific NER model (e.g., spaCy `en_core_web_trf`).

**S3. 🌀 After running EntityDuplicationDebugger, graph loses important entity relationships.**

*Fix:* Merge is deleting the alias entity without redirecting its edges. Fix: `merge_duplicate_entities()` must rebuild relationship store with canonical names. Test merge on small subset first.

**S4. 🐢 Neo4j BFS query times out on a graph with 500K nodes.**

*Fix:* Use Cypher APOC path expander with `bfs: true, limit: 100`. Add index on entity `name` property. Set `maxPathLength: 3`. Use `PROFILE` to identify slow query plans.

**S5. 💸 LightRAG indexing hits OpenAI rate limits on 10,000 documents.**

*Fix:* Reduce `max_async` from default to 2. Add exponential backoff: `tenacity.retry(wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=4, max=60))`. Batch documents in groups of 100 with 10-second delays.

**S6. 🦠 Global search returns outdated CEO names after executive changes.**

*Fix:* Document timestamp is newer than community report timestamp. Implement document-hash-triggered community re-summarisation. Add `last_updated` field to community reports. Set `max_age_days=7`.

**S7. 🎭 Hybrid mode always gives same answer regardless of query specificity.**

*Fix:* Global mode (relationship search) dominates hybrid result. Reduce `top_k_global` to 10. Add query-type classifier to route specific queries to local-only mode. Add entity type filter to hybrid context.

**S8. ⚖️ Graph RAG always returns answers about "Apple Inc." regardless of topic.**

*Fix:* Apple is a hub node (high degree) dominating PageRank. Apply diversity-aware scoring with `rarity_bonus`. Add entity exclusion list for known hubs when not relevant. Use PPR seeded from query — not global PageRank.

**S9. 💥 LLM returns "I cannot answer" for every query after context compression.**

*Fix:* Token budget too aggressive — reduced context to 500 tokens (below useful threshold). Increase budget to at least 2000 tokens. Ensure entity descriptions are included before text passages in context order.

**S10. 🔗 Graph has entities but no relationships — completely disconnected.**

*Fix:* Relationship extraction prompt was accidentally removed in a config update. Restore relationships section to extraction prompt. Add health check that alerts if `avg_degree < 1` after any indexing run.
